Find the value of $k$ for the parabola $y=5{x}^{2}+kx-8,$ shown above.

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since the graph tells us that the axis of symmetry is $x=-2,$ we will set our result equal to $-2.$ 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=5$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{k}{2(5)} \\  & =-\frac{k}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-2,$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k}{10} & =-2 \\ -k & =-20 \\ k & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
